claims.text: While a readiness probe fails, the container is not ready, the Pod shows 0/1 under READY, and Services that select it do not send it traffic (it is removed from their endpoints); the container is not restarted.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Lifecycle (readinessProbe: endpoints controller removes the Pod's IP); Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes

claims.text: When the readiness probe passes again the Pod is added back to the Service's endpoints and gets traffic again.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes (readiness probes run for the whole lifecycle)

claims.text: A container with no readiness probe is treated as ready (default state Success) as soon as it runs.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Lifecycle ('If a container does not provide a readiness probe, the default state is Success')

claims.text: A Deployment counts a Pod available once it is ready (minReadySeconds 0 by default); a rolling update removes old Pods only within maxUnavailable of available Pods.
With replicas 2 and default maxSurge/maxUnavailable 25% (surge 1, unavailable 0), a new Pod that never becomes ready stops the rollout: no old Pod is removed and the update never completes.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Deployments (Max Surge/Max Unavailable rounding; progress); outputs readiness.txt
